title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRDs, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing - Q2 2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Executive summary:

This page consolidates the product overview, prioritized PRDs and requirements, key design decisions, roadmap themes for Q2-Q4 2026, and pricing & packaging guidance for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and GTM stakeholders.

## 1. Product overview

Unified Inference is Redwood Inference's integrated product strategy to provide a single developer experience and control plane for inference across hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The initiative focuses on delivering predictable latency, cost controls, and operational tooling that are consistent across environments.

Objectives (top-level):
- Make inference predictable: latency SLOs, per-route cost insights, and deterministic throughput for reserved capacity.
- Reduce unit economics: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations integrated into the product controls.
- Enterprise readiness: private deployments, KMS integration, and auditability.
- Developer experience: simple SDKs, streaming, function calling, and rollout controls.

User personas:
- ML engineers: model selection, quantization, evaluation harnesses.
- Platform engineers: capacity planning, routing policies, infra cost reports.
- Product engineers: low-latency chat/generation APIs and feature rollout controls.

Key offerings summarized:
- Hosted API: pay-as-you-go with streaming and tool-calls.
- Dedicated: committed GPU pools with SLA-backed latency targets.
- Private: customer-managed network option with audit logs and KMS/HSM integration.

## 2. PRD summary and prioritized requirements

Purpose: Provide a single source of truth for product requirements and acceptance criteria for the next two releases (v1.3 and v2.0).

Scope (in-scope):
- Unified routing policy configuration (by latency/cost/region)
- Prefix/KV cache controls exposed to customers
- Batching and autoscaling policies for Dedicated fleets
- Pricing meter for mixed-mode calls (embedding + generation)
- Rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback)

Out-of-scope for v1.3 (target v2.0+):
- Full multi-tenant private control plane (advanced RBAC)
- Predictive pre-warming via historical workload modeling

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
1) Customers can configure per-route latency SLO and be routed automatically to compatible variants if SLO cannot be met.
2) Dedicated customers can set a max-batch-latency and min-throughput target; system honors targets within 15% during normal load.
3) Pricing meter computes per-request charge for multi-model or multi-modal calls within 2% of expected estimate.

Requirements table (priority, id, requirement, acceptance):
| Priority | ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|---|
| P0 | PRD-001 | Per-route latency SLO config and smart routing | 100% of routes can set SLO; routing fallback triggers and logs when SLO breached |
| P0 | PRD-002 | KV/prefix cache controls in Console and API | API to enable/disable cache per-model; cache-hit metrics shown in console |
| P1 | PRD-003 | Dedicated autoscaling policy UI + API | Policies can be saved and simulated in staging; scaling events logged |
| P1 | PRD-004 | Unified pricing meter for mixed calls | Billing preview available in console and via API for sample workloads |
| P2 | PRD-005 | Canary/A-B rollout controls with automatic rollback | 2-stage rollout and automatic rollback on regression metric |

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency p95 budget: Hosted API p95 <= 120ms for small-context text-generation (<=512 tokens) on curated models.
- Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime per month for committed pools.
- Observability: per-token cost, latency, and cache-hit rate visible with 1m resolution for 30d.

## 3. Design specs and architecture decisions

Design principles:
- Failure isolation: fallbacks should avoid cascading failures across customers.
- Deterministic performance: prefer bounded batching and prefixed cache paths to reduce variance.
- Cost transparency: expose unit economics as first-class telemetry.

High level design (text):
- Control plane: unified config API (routes, SLOs, pricing rules) backed by a hierarchical policy store. Configs propagate to serving via streaming delta updates.
- Serving plane: model-adapter runtime that implements kernel selection, KV cache logic, batching scheduler, and quantization-aware execution.
- Router: policy engine evaluates SLOs, cost constraints and capacity signals to select target pool/model variant.
- Billing: event-driven billing meter that normalizes mixed-modal usage into billing units and exports daily aggregates.

Key design decisions (ADRs):
- ADR-2026-04: Use hierarchical policy precedence (route > org > global) to allow per-team overrides. Decision: approved.
- ADR-2026-06: Batching scheduler will implement max-batch-latency over fixed batch-size to honor latency SLOs. Decision: approved.
- ADR-2026-07: Billing units defined as token-generation units + embedding units with an exchange rate maintained in the pricing config. Decision: approved.

API contract examples (curl snippets):
- Create route with latency SLO:

  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"chat/support","slo":{"p95_ms":120,"priority":"high"},"fallback_policy":[{"variant":"gpt-4o-lite","when":"slo_miss"}] }'

- Pricing preview request (JSON):

  POST /v1/pricing/preview
  {
    "calls": [
      { "type":"generation", "model":"openLM/gptx-13b", "prompt_tokens":120, "completion_tokens":250 },
      { "type":"embedding", "model":"text-embed-002", "tokens":130 }
    ]
  }

## 4. UX and Console changes

Console pages to add/update:
- Route config page: new SLO card, fallback rules UI, historical SLO compliance chart.
- Dedicated fleet page: autoscaling policy editor, simulate policy button, cost estimate.
- Pricing preview page: sample workload builder + export to CSV.
- Release/rollout page: visualize canary cohorts, regression triggers, and quick rollback buttons.

UX considerations:
- Default SLOs should be conservative to avoid noisy incidents.
- Provide a guided setup for Dedicated customers that teaches how to set min-throughput and max-batch-latency.

## 5. Roadmap & themes (Q2 2026 - Q4 2026)

Themes by quarter:
- Q2 2026 (current): Core routing + SLOs, cache controls, baseline pricing meter, console SLO visuals. (v1.3 target)
- Q3 2026: Dedicated autoscaling policies, rollout controls, billing preview API GA. (v2.0 target)
- Q4 2026: Private control plane enhancements (RBAC), predictive pre-warming POC, cross-region routing for failover. (v2.1/v3.0 follow-ups)

Milestones & dates (planned):
1) 2026-05-15 - v1.3 beta: SLO routing and cache controls in staging, selected customers onboarded.
2) 2026-06-30 - v1.3 GA: Console and API for SLOs, cache control, pricing preview beta.
3) 2026-09-15 - v2.0 beta: Dedicated autoscaling UI + API, rollout controls beta.
4) 2026-11-20 - v2.0 GA: Autoscaling and rollout GA, billing preview GA.

Dependencies:
- Eng-serving-runtime: batching scheduler, KV cache instrumentation (owner: runtime team).
- Eng-sre: capacity planning and Dedicated SLA runbooks.
- Finance: billing unit exchange rates and tax logic exposure.

## 6. Pricing & packaging notes

Goals for pricing: be predictable for Dedicated customers (monthly commit) and transparent for Hosted usage (per-token + per-embedding). Offer additive discounts for pre-committed Dedicated usage and private deployments.

Suggested packaging tiers (summary):
- Pay-as-you-go (Hosted): per-token generation price + per-embedding price. No commit. Basic support.
- Dedicated Standard: monthly commit, guaranteed baseline throughput, standard SLA, 10% discount on token rate within commit.
- Dedicated Enterprise: annual contract, tighter SLOs, premium support, dedicated account engineering.
- Private: platform license + per-node runtime fees + professional services for on-prem.

Pricing examples (illustrative only):
| Tier | Metric | Unit price 
|---|---|---:|
| Hosted | Generation | $0.0009 / token |
| Hosted | Embedding | $0.0005 / embedding unit |
| Dedicated (committed) | Generation within commit | $0.0006 / token |

Mixed-call billing logic:
- Normalize embeddings to token-equivalent units using a configurable exchange rate (default: 1 embedding = 200 token-units).
- Billing preview API should show per-call breakdown and total estimated daily cost.

Discount mechanics and trials:
- 30-day trial credit for new accounts up to $500 usage.
- Early adopter pricing program for Dedicated customers that commit before 2026-08-01.

## 7. Release notes (v1.3 beta & GA highlights)

v1.3 beta (2026-05-15):
- Added per-route latency SLO configuration with smart routing fallback.
- Exposed prefix/KV cache toggle and cache-hit metrics in Console.
- Pricing preview API introduced (beta).
- Known limitations: Dedicated autoscaling not yet exposed; billing preview estimates may differ by up to 5% for complex mixed workloads.

v1.3 GA (planned 2026-06-30):
- Hardened SLO routing and fallback policies.
- Console SLO history charts and alerting integration.
- Pricing preview moved to GA for single-model calls; mixed-call GA planned for v2.0.

## 8. Operational rollout and runbook pointers

Rollout checklist (numbered):
1) Run integration tests in staging with 3 customer-like workloads.
2) Warm Dedicated pools with representative load to validate autoscaler behavior.
3) Run a 48-hour canary on 2 production organizations with monitoring for SLO regressions.
4) Enable GA and increase customer onboarding in waves of 25 orgs per day.

Runbooks and owners:
- SLO-miss incident runbook: eng-sre/runbooks/slo-miss.md (owner: eng-sre).
- Billing discrepancy investigation: finance-and-legal/billing-discrepancy-playbook (owner: finance).
- Dedicated capacity shortage: eng-sre/capacity-planning/shortage-procedure (owner: eng-sre).

## 9. Success metrics and KPIs

Primary KPIs:
- SLO compliance: % of routes meeting p95 target (target >= 99% after GA).
- Cost per 1M tokens across typical workloads (target decrease of 18% for customers using caching/ batching guidance).
- Dedicated renewal rate for customers after 6 months (target >= 85%).
- Time-to-onboard for Dedicated customers (target <= 5 business days).

Secondary metrics:
- Console adoption of pricing-preview (50% of new accounts use during first 7 days).
- Number of rollbacks triggered during canary (target <= 2 per quarter).

## 10. Ownership, next steps and open questions

Owners:
- Product lead: Aisha Patel (product)
- Runtime integration owner: Marco Alvarez (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE owner: Priya Nair (eng-sre)
- Finance lead: Daniel Brooks (finance-and-legal)

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize API schema for pricing-preview (due 2026-03-20).
- Kickoff UI designs for SLO route page and Dedicated autoscaling (due 2026-03-30).
- Align on billing exchange rate for embeddings (finance + product by 2026-04-05).

Open questions:
- What is the default embedding-to-token exchange rate for billing? (proposal: 200 token-units per embedding).
- Can we auto-suggest batch/throughput settings for Dedicated customers based on sample workload in console?
- Should rollout metrics be part of the default alerting set for all customers or only Enterprise?
